comparator.name: Computer Science
components: Genuine minor/free-choice space; no subject invented.
Required independent computer-science research and development project.
Selected 6-EC advanced option; requires fluent C/C++ programming and attendance.

routeSelection.basis: Standard standalone Computer Science route, first corresponding current route; Informatica en Economie excluded. First eligible current 6-EC restricted option selected in official list order, independently of UCR fit.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Programming, software engineering, databases, operating systems, networks and computer systems
Algorithms, data structures, formal reasoning and computational problem-solving
Mathematical foundations of computing: discrete mathematics, calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics
Data science, machine learning, data mining, visualisation and prediction
Artificial-intelligence reasoning, optimisation, learning and intelligent-system design
Computer-science research methods, team software work, scientific problem-solving and an independent bachelor thesis
adjacent: Responsible deployment and human-facing applications of computational systems
Computational applications in visual and intelligent systems
questions: How do algorithms, software and systems turn real problems into reliable computation?
How can data-driven and intelligent systems be designed, evaluated and used responsibly?

trace: Research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments, statistical inference and an original team data project supply specific empirical computational-research preparation, not a dedicated CS thesis.

Ethical frameworks, fairness, privacy, accountability and human-AI interaction directly support responsible computing; overlap with current Leiden AI and Ethics is substantive, without imported Philosophy & AI units.
Bayesian inference, temporal probabilistic models, decision theory, Markov decisions, partial observability and multi-agent interaction implement probabilistic intelligent-agent decisions.
Formal logic, sets, Boolean algebra, relations, direct/indirect proof, induction and recursive structures directly supply discrete computational reasoning.

Uninformed/heuristic/adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, continuous/discrete optimisation and linear programming with algorithm implementation and experimental projects directly implement computational search and optimisation.
Reinforcement-learning frameworks, algorithm implementation and neural trial-and-error agents directly develop intelligent learning systems; no inferred biological-cognition content.
Internet layers/protocols plus processes, scheduling, concurrency, memory and storage, packet investigation and system-performance projects directly implement systems infrastructure.
Relational theory, SQL, authorisation, normalisation and query processing directly implement database study; full stated scope considered.
C++ and Haskell, types/recursion/classes, version control, testing, debugging, code review and design patterns implement software-construction methods; not a guaranteed client-based software house.
Algorithms/data structures, sorting/search/graphs, computability/verification/reductions/complexity classes and measured performance projects directly supply algorithmic theory and research.

Algebraic/number-theoretic algorithms, fast arithmetic, hashing, dynamic programming and network flows develop mathematical algorithm design and experimental optimisation; not the entire dedicated formal complexity unit.
Data import, cleaning/transformation/joining, textual/spatial data, visualisation, web scraping and own research project directly support scientific data inquiry.
Regression/classification, resampling/regularisation, nonlinear models, trees/SVM/unsupervised learning and predictive evaluation on real data directly implement machine learning.

Representations, filtering, segmentation/features, tracking/classification, Python/OpenCV and unseen-image benchmarking develop actual computational vision, not image-generation/rendering equivalence.

Neural-network theory, Python/Keras/TensorFlow implementation, backpropagation, regularisation/evaluation and vision/text/time-series projects directly implement deep learning and empirical model research.
Python structured and object-oriented programming, recursion, tests and debugging directly implement computational problem solving.
Functions, limits, differentiation, integration, equations and numerical/dynamic modelling with Mathematica supply calculus and computational-modelling tools.
Matrices, vector spaces, transformations, eigenvalues, least squares/SVD and applications to signals/dynamics/PCA directly supply computational linear algebra.
Root finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation/quadrature/ODE and linear/nonlinear systems, with convergence/stability/error experiments, supply specific numerical-computing methods.
Signals, convolution, Fourier/frequency representations, sampling/reconstruction and feedback with computational applications support mathematical analysis of information-processing systems.
Probability spaces/random variables, multivariate distributions, inference, likelihood/Bayesian reasoning and sampling-algorithm experiments directly support rigorous probabilistic computing.
Experimental-design knowledge and multivariable model selection/diagnosis/interpretation with data-analysis reports and poster supply specific applied statistical methods for empirical computing.

AI capabilities/limitations, applications, workforce/economic effects, governance and regulation, plus AI-readiness research, support specific deployment analysis alongside technical intelligent-system design.

alternatives.label: Computer science, data and intelligent systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed composition has twenty computing and mathematical courses, applied statistical research, AI deployment analysis and mandatory personal/professional development. The label states those actual priorities.
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, algorithms, software development, databases, operating systems and networks with mathematical and statistical methods. Machine learning, computer vision, neural networks, optimisation and reinforcement learning develop intelligent-system design and evaluation. Applied statistical analysis and the study of AI’s organisational and societal use add specific methodological and deployment perspectives. Dedicated hardware design, computer architecture, technical security and a compulsory thesis remain important differences from Leiden.
progression: Current offerings and formal prerequisites checked for all placements. Programming and calculus precede required advanced courses; at least six 300-level courses, four per term, 24 unique selections and Year-1 PPD. Retained foundation-before-advanced sequencing where feasible; no invented formal prerequisites. Machine Learning has no formal prerequisite; its mathematical preparation remains advisory.

candidates.label: Data science and statistical learning
candidates.reason: Strongest completed core already includes data preparation, probability/statistics, multivariable modelling, machine learning, computer vision, neural networks and research. Current remaining advanced calculus/robotics courses do not yield four genuinely different target-relevant course choices. Manufacturing the difference with broad brain, social or philosophical courses would not create a justified data-science response.

selection.assessment: One qualified core response retained after strengthening actual computational content and methods. Data/ML candidate fails substantive distinctness: its actual central content is already in the strongest core; two omitted active computing courses do not create four genuine course changes. Stop after alternative2fails. Historical cognition-heavythirdproposal separately reassessed and withdrawn: current standardCS sources do not substantiate its claimed mandatory ComputationalCognitiveNeuroscience/PhilosophyAI/MathematicalModelling courses; HCI/NLP electives alone do not justify whole biological-cognition trajectory. No alternatives manufactured to reachthree, and no academic no-match inferred from planning coverage.

blocks: Both develop foundational programming and computational problem solving. UCR uses Python with structured and object-oriented techniques, testing and debugging; Leiden develops working C++ knowledge, algorithms and software-engineering principles.
Both cover operating-system resource management and Internet architecture and protocols through practical computational work.
Both cover relational databases, SQL, data modelling, normalization and query processing.

Both develop advanced programming, testing, software design and version-control practice. UCR uses C++ and Haskell with code review and documentation; Leiden additionally includes Bash, build systems, APIs and low-level programming.
Both develop efficient algorithms and data structures, their implementation and performance analysis. UCR also treats computability and complexity classes within this course.

Both use algorithmic problem-solving methods, including greedy methods, dynamic programming and graph/network algorithms, with implementation and analysis. UCR extends into advanced algebraic and number-theoretic algorithms.
UCR does not offer a dedicated digital logic and hardware-design course.
UCR's Networks & Operating Systems discusses hardware/software interaction but does not reproduce a dedicated computer-architecture course.
UCR Software Development uses C++ and Haskell but does not reproduce Leiden's separate programming-language-concepts component.
UCR includes responsible-computing and systems perspectives but no dedicated technical cybersecurity course in the fixed portfolio.

UCR Software Development includes design, testing, version control and code review and is represented with Programming Techniques. No further course supplies the client-based software-house project, requirements, project management and deployment of this separate Leiden unit.

UCR Algorithms & Data Structures includes complexity classes and reductions and is represented with Data Structures. This additional formal-complexity unit retains separate credit; Advanced Algorithms is represented with algorithmic problem solving.
Both establish calculus and mathematical problem-solving used in computing.
Both cover matrices, vector spaces, transformations and eigenvalues.
Both establish probability distributions, inference and probabilistic reasoning for computing.
Both provide logic and discrete structures for formal computational reasoning.
No single UCR course reproduces Leiden's dedicated theoretical Foundations of Computer Science module.
UCR has no dedicated automata-theory component.

UCR Algorithms & Data Structures includes computability, verification and reductions and is represented with the data-structures unit. It does not provide an additional dedicated formal-languages/automata course row.
UCR offers one logic-and-discrete-mathematics course rather than Leiden's two-stage logic sequence.

UCR Mathematical Methods includes integral calculus and differential equations and is represented with Calculus 1. Its single course row is not duplicated for this additional separately credited calculus unit.
Data science, machine learning & artificial intelligence
Both teach regression, classification, clustering and evaluation of predictive models.
Both examine fairness, responsibility, privacy and ethical questions raised by artificial intelligence.
Both cover computational search, optimisation and reasoning for artificial intelligence.

Image processing and vision analyse images, whereas this elective emphasises generating 3D graphics, transformations, projection, shading and rendering in C/C++. No selected dedicated graphics counterpart.

Both develop statistical analysis and model-based inference. UCR includes experimental-design knowledge and multivariable models with practical data-analysis reporting; Leiden applies the methods within computer science.

Both prepare students to set up and report empirical investigations. UCR develops research design, sampling, statistics and an original data project. Leiden explicitly emphasises academic writing, presenting, finding and evaluating sources, and setting up and reporting experiments within computer science.

Both support the start of university study through academic writing, presenting, collaboration and study development. UCR additionally includes personal development and civic engagement; Leiden situates these skills within LIACS.
UCR has no scheduled bachelor-thesis course; the standardized optional independent-research opportunity is placed against this component.
Leiden's genuine 30-EC minor or free-choice space is preserved without inventing a subject.

Leiden surveys computer-science research areas, the academic/business landscape and societal impact through creative teamwork and scientific communication. Related UCR technical projects contribute such skills, but no unused course supplies this dedicated disciplinary orientation.

notes.text: The UCR composition provides substantial computing and AI study, but does not include separate dedicated hardware-design, computer-architecture or technical-cybersecurity courses. The composition is not the same disciplinary degree or an automatic qualification for further study.

Leiden’s compulsory 15-EC thesis and 30-EC open-choice space remain distinct. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC, requires separate approval, and is not an automatic substitute for the Leiden thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden Computer Science combines programming and software with algorithms, mathematical foundations, computer systems, data and artificial intelligence. The degree develops practical and theoretical problem solving and concludes with an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers a qualified composition in computer science, data and intelligent systems. It combines software, algorithms, databases, networks and operating systems with mathematics, statistical research and substantial AI study. It does not reproduce the dedicated digital-hardware, computer-architecture and technical-security sequence, or the compulsory Leiden thesis. The data and AI content is integrated into this composition rather than presented again as a separate option.

curriculum.limitation: Years one and two each contain 60 EC of required study. Year three contains 30 EC of open choice, a selected 6-EC advanced option, AI and Ethics (3 EC), Software Engineering (6 EC) and the thesis project (15 EC). Computer Graphics is the illustrated advanced option and requires fluent C/C++ programming and attendance. Its autumn placement alongside 30 EC of open choice gives 36 EC in autumn and 24 EC in spring. The thesis includes a compulsory bachelor class and matching in November–December. By 1 February, students need the full 60-EC first year, at least 66 EC from years two and three, completed Research Methods, and no more than 27 EC of outstanding upper-year spring courses excluding the thesis; a September precheck also applies. It includes a proposal, peer review, progress presentation, draft review, final report and presentation under LIACS supervision and a second assessor. Open choice can use an eligible Leiden–Delft–Rotterdam minor or five CS electives; other packages require approval and overlapping content must be replaced.
